title: Linkability of homeowner identity to enrolled devices
description: During account registration and device enrollment, the homeowner's identity becomes linked to their cameras and sensors. This creates a persistent link that could enable tracking of the homeowner's activities across devices and over time.
assumptions: The Home Hub stores associations between account credentials and device identifiers

title: Identifiability of homeowner during registration
description: The registration process requires the homeowner to provide identifying information (account credentials, device serial numbers, etc.), making them directly identifiable in the system.
assumptions: Registration requires unique identifiers for account and device enrollment

title: Disclosure of sensitive registration data
description: Account credentials, device information, and potentially location data transmitted during registration could be intercepted or disclosed to unauthorized parties.
assumptions: Data is transmitted over network during registration process

title: Data aggregation from registration and device enrollment
description: Multiple data points collected during registration (account info, device types, quantities, potentially location) can be aggregated to create a comprehensive profile of the homeowner and their smart home setup.
assumptions: Home Hub stores all registration and enrollment data in a unified profile

title: Unawareness of data collection scope
description: Homeowner may not be fully aware of what data is collected during registration, how it will be used, stored, or shared with third parties.
assumptions: Privacy policy may not be prominently displayed or clearly explained during registration

title: Non-compliance with privacy regulations
description: Registration process may not comply with privacy regulations (GDPR, CCPA, etc.) regarding consent mechanisms, data minimization, or transparency requirements.
assumptions: System may not implement proper consent management or data handling practices
uncertainty_note: Depends on specific implementation of consent and data handling

title: Guest presence detectable through access code entry
description: An observer could detect that a guest is using the system by watching them enter a temporary access code at the Home Hub, or by monitoring network traffic between the guest device and Home Hub. The door unlocking action itself also reveals guest presence.
assumptions: Physical observation or network monitoring is possible

title: Access code disclosure through shoulder surfing or interception
description: The temporary access code entered by the guest could be observed by unauthorized parties through shoulder surfing at the Home Hub interface, or intercepted during transmission if not properly encrypted.
assumptions: Physical proximity or network access by attackers

title: Guest unaware of data collection during access
description: The guest may not be aware that their access attempt is being logged, including metadata such as timestamp, access code used, and door unlock status. They may not understand what data is retained or how long.
assumptions: No clear privacy notice provided to guests

title: Access attempts linkable to guest identity
description: The temporary access code could be linked to the guest's identity in the Home Hub's logs, allowing correlation of this access with other activities, times, or locations of the same guest.
assumptions: Access codes are associated with guest identities in system records

title: Guest cannot deny access attempt
description: If the Home Hub logs the access code entry and door unlock event, the guest cannot later deny that they accessed the front door at that specific time, which could have privacy implications.
assumptions: System maintains audit logs of access events

title: Event Linkability to Individuals
description: Motion, door, and sensor events written to the local log could be linked to specific individuals based on timing, location, and patterns of activity within the home.
assumptions: The event log contains sufficient contextual data (timestamps, sensor IDs) to enable correlation with individual behavior.

title: Individual Identifiability from Event Patterns
description: Aggregated event data in the local log could enable identification of specific individuals through behavioral patterns, occupancy schedules, and movement patterns.
assumptions: Event data includes sufficient granularity (time, location) to distinguish between different household members.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Event Log
description: If the local event log is not properly secured, unauthorized parties could access sensitive information about home occupancy, door access, and movement patterns.
assumptions: The local event log may be accessible via network or physical access without adequate authentication controls.

title: Data Aggregation Revealing Behavioral Patterns
description: Multiple motion, door, and sensor events aggregated over time in the local log could reveal detailed behavioral patterns, daily routines, and occupancy schedules of household members.
assumptions: The event log retains historical data that can be analyzed to identify patterns over time.

title: User Unawareness of Event Logging
description: Users may be unaware of what specific events are being logged, how long they are retained, or what inferences can be drawn from the event data.
assumptions: The system may not provide clear transparency about data collection practices to end users.

title: Lack of User Control Over Event Data
description: Users may have limited or no control over what events are logged, how long they are retained, or the ability to delete or modify their event history.
assumptions: The system may not provide user-facing controls for managing event log data.

title: Linkability of video clips to specific home/user
description: Video clips uploaded from Home Hub to cloud storage can be linked to a specific household or user identity through metadata, account associations, or device identifiers, enabling tracking of which home generated which video content.
assumptions: Cloud storage maintains user account associations with uploaded content

title: Identifiability of individuals in video content
description: Recorded camera clips may contain identifiable individuals (faces, license plates, etc.) that could be used to identify specific people, their activities, or locations when stored in cloud video storage.
assumptions: Camera clips contain visual data that can identify people or objects

title: Unauthorized disclosure of video clips from cloud storage
description: Video clips stored in cloud video storage could be accessed by unauthorized parties through security breaches, insider threats, or misconfigured access controls, leading to privacy violations.
assumptions: Cloud storage has potential security vulnerabilities or access control issues

title: Aggregation of video clips to create detailed behavioral profiles
description: Multiple video clips stored over time in cloud storage could be aggregated to create comprehensive profiles of household activities, routines, visitor patterns, and behavioral data beyond individual clip context.
assumptions: Cloud storage retains multiple clips over extended periods

title: User unawareness of data upload scope and retention
description: Users may not be fully aware of what video data is being uploaded to cloud storage, how long it is retained, or what processing occurs on the stored clips, limiting informed consent.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not clearly communicate upload scope and retention policies

title: Non-compliance with data protection regulations
description: Storage of video clips containing personal data in cloud storage may violate GDPR, CCPA, or other privacy regulations if proper legal basis, data subject rights, or cross-border transfer mechanisms are not in place.
assumptions: Video clips contain personal data subject to privacy regulations
uncertainty_note: Depends on jurisdiction and specific compliance measures implemented

title: Motion alert data excessively exposed to backend
description: The Home Hub forwards real-time motion alerts to the Mobile App Backend. This transfer may expose more personal data than necessary (e.g., precise timing, frequency, and location of motion events) beyond what is strictly required for the alert functionality. The data could reveal occupancy patterns, daily routines, and presence/absence of individuals in the home.
assumptions: Motion alerts contain timestamped location data that could be used to infer occupancy patterns and personal routines.

title: Motion data reveals occupancy and behavioral patterns
description: The motion alert transmitted from Home Hub to Mobile App Backend may disclose information about when individuals are present or absent from the home, their movement patterns, and daily routines. This information could be used to infer sensitive personal details about the household.
assumptions: Motion detection data includes sufficient granularity to infer occupancy and behavioral patterns.

title: Motion alerts linkable to specific individuals or households
description: Motion alert data transmitted to the backend could be linked to specific individuals or households, especially when combined with other data sources. This linkability could enable profiling or tracking of individuals' presence and movement patterns.
assumptions: The motion alert data contains identifiers or can be correlated with other data to identify specific individuals or households.

title: Unauthorized interception of motion detection notifications
description: Motion-detected notifications transmitted from the mobile app backend to the homeowner's phone could be intercepted by unauthorized parties during transmission, revealing when motion was detected at the property and potentially indicating occupancy patterns.
assumptions: Notifications are transmitted over network connections that could be vulnerable to interception

title: Aggregation of notification data reveals occupancy patterns
description: Multiple motion detection notifications over time could be aggregated to build a profile of the homeowner's presence patterns, daily routines, and when the property is occupied or vacant.
assumptions: Notifications are logged or could be collected by third parties over time

title: Linkability of notifications to homeowner identity
description: Motion detection notifications could be linked to the homeowner's identity and other data about their property, enabling correlation with other activities or data sources.
assumptions: Notification delivery is tied to identifiable homeowner accounts

title: Linkability of aggregated analytics to individual users
description: The cloud analytics vendor could potentially link aggregated device-usage analytics back to individual users through pattern analysis, especially if the aggregation level is insufficient or if unique usage patterns exist.
assumptions: Aggregated data may contain quasi-identifiers or unique behavioral patterns that enable re-linking to individuals

title: Re-identification risk from analytics data
description: Even with aggregation, the analytics vendor could potentially re-identify individual users by combining the shared data with other datasets they possess or through statistical inference attacks.
assumptions: Vendor may have access to additional data sources that could be combined with analytics data

title: Unauthorized disclosure of analytics data
description: The cloud analytics vendor could disclose the shared device-usage analytics to unauthorized third parties, or use the data beyond the agreed purpose without user consent.
assumptions: Vendor may have incentives to monetize or share data beyond original agreement

title: User unawareness of third-party data sharing
description: Mobile app users may not be adequately informed that their device-usage analytics are being shared with an external cloud analytics vendor, or may not understand the extent of data sharing.
assumptions: Privacy policy may not clearly disclose third-party analytics sharing or users may not read it

title: Non-compliance with privacy regulations
description: The data sharing arrangement with the cloud analytics vendor may not comply with applicable privacy regulations (GDPR, CCPA, etc.) regarding data transfers, purpose limitation, or vendor due diligence.
assumptions: Data sharing may involve cross-border transfers or lack proper legal basis

title: Unauthorized disclosure of video content during retrieval
description: Video clips retrieved from cloud storage to the mobile app backend could be intercepted or accessed by unauthorized parties during the data transfer, exposing sensitive footage of the homeowner's property.
assumptions: Video clips contain personally identifiable information and sensitive property footage

title: Identifiability through video content retrieval
description: Retrieved video clips may contain identifiable information about the homeowner, their family members, or visitors, which could be exposed if the retrieval process is compromised.
assumptions: Video footage contains visual identifiers of individuals

title: Linkability of retrieval patterns to user behavior
description: Patterns of video clip retrieval could be correlated to infer homeowner behavior, presence at home, or daily routines, enabling profiling through access metadata.
assumptions: Retrieval timestamps and frequency are logged and could be analyzed

title: Violation of storage limitation principle
description: Video clips may be retrieved and processed even when no longer needed for the original purpose, or retention policies may not be properly enforced during the retrieval process.
assumptions: Storage limitation policies exist but may not be enforced during retrieval
uncertainty_note: Context Nc.1.1.4 from retrieved knowledge may be approximate for this specific flow
